route: persistent identity, provenance bundles, ontology identifiers, and explicit version relations
semantic_novelty_after_deduplication: RAKL must distinguish full fiber identity from its numeric namespace slot because the latter is used operationally as a stable allocation namespace.
A repaired collision remains provenance history rather than being erased by renaming.
Alias/revision relations are typed reconciliation objects; semantic similarity alone cannot establish identity.

prior_art.projection: PROV represents entities, derivations, revisions, specializations and named provenance bundles; changing bundle assertions produces a distinct bundle.
prior_art.effect_on_claim: Generic provenance-aware identity/versioning is prior art.

prior_art.projection: A URI alone can be insufficient to identify a particular description of an entity in a specific provenance bundle; cross-bundle mention is explicit.
prior_art.effect_on_claim: Supports keeping historical definition context explicit rather than treating a reused label as self-identifying.

prior_art.projection: Ontology elements are uniquely identified and short identifiers map in a well-defined way to persistent URLs.
prior_art.effect_on_claim: Stable namespace allocation is established practice; RAKL's narrower contribution is applying fail-closed reconciliation to its self-R&D fiber ledger.

prior_art.projection: Different versions are linked through explicit typed relations such as IsNewVersionOf and IsPreviousVersionOf rather than silently replacing resource identity.
prior_art.effect_on_claim: Explicit version/alias edges are prior art and should be reused rather than claimed as novel.

deduplicated_conclusion: No new universal identity theory is claimed. The retained RAKL method object is a deterministic, authority-non-escalating self-registry check that treats namespace collisions, provenance identity, aliases, orphans and cycles as closure blockers and preserves their repair history.
